Thank you for all your hard work and effort. The development my child has made in the short time he has been with you has been outstanding. His personality has developed, his vocabulary has increased, he loves his teachers, he is interested in education and so motivated to attend school.
Reception Parent at Eastcourt
We are very grateful to Eastcourt school for the educational foundation they have provided to both of our children, particularly given some of the challenges they have experienced around maths skills. For this reason we were keen to offer our perspective of high level of teaching and support at the school. Our eldest daughter, who is now in year 7, was provided with dedicated maths support throughout her school years, particularly in year 6, where she was given additional 1-2-1 support and a specialised programme to help prepare her for the challenges of secondary school. This was incredibly successful and she is now in a higher maths set and able to maintain the pace of work, which was previously difficult for her. Both my daughters have very fond memories of their time at Eastcourt, the kindness of pupils and teachers as well as the openly supportive environment. The efforts of all teaching staff, firstly highlighting this area of difficulty and then working closely with us and our daughter really has made all of the difference and we believe that the confidence she has in maths today would not have been achievable without the team at Eastcourt school. Eastcourt is like a family that we will always value.
Parents of a child currently at Eastcourt and an Eastcourtonian
Personally, Eastcourt really prepared me for my secondary school, Brentwood (especially year 6). For example most of the curriculum from Year 6 was very similar to my Year 7 and I even found that some things I knew girls in my class didn’t know because I learnt them from Eastcourt. I did a filtration topic in chemistry and I ended up doing really well in that topic because I knew lots about it from yr 6. I was prepared for the homework because Year 7 was the equivalent to the amount in Year 6 at Eastcourt. So while other people struggled with homework I was prepared for the workload. Since reception Eastcourt managed to maintain a healthy competitive nature which helped me achieve some of the best results. When I was in Year 5 the number challenges were introduced for both problem solving and quick maths which really improved the maths skills of many of us in my class. I really enjoyed my time at Eastcourt and I had an amazing experience. I would really recommend future children to come here.'
I attended Eastcourt Independent School from ages 6 to 11, and I look back incredibly fondly on my time there. It was a place where I thrived both academically and extracurricularly, supported by the excellent teachers and spurred on by the wide range of activities the school offered, I took up public speaking and drama, joined the school netball team and played in tournaments, alongside studying. With the support of the teaching staff and Eastcourt's positive environment, I secured places at all the secondary schools I applied to, including scholarships for Chigwell and Forest School.

Welcome to Eastcourt Independent School
At Eastcourt, we believe that every child is a unique individual, valued for who they are and encouraged to realise their full potential. Our dedicated staff create a safe, nurturing, and stimulating environment where pupils develop not only a passion for learning, but also the qualities of kindness, resilience, and self-confidence.
We place great importance on building strong partnerships with parents and carers, recognising that a close collaboration between home and school is essential in helping each child flourish academically, socially, and personally.
Whether you are visiting us online or in person, I hope you gain a genuine sense of the warmth, energy, and ambition that make Eastcourt such an exceptional place for children to learn, grow, and thrive.

Our Commitment to Excellence
Eastcourt Independent School is a private day school for boys and girls from 4-11 years old. It has no religious affiliation – we value parents and pupils of all faiths and none. It is our intention that our school aims to work with parents to help children grow into caring, well-educated individuals who have a good understanding and strong commitment to develop personal qualities that help the society in which we live, an appreciation of others, and tolerance and compassion to build a positive future.​

Our Curriculum
At Eastcourt School, we provide a creative curriculum which maximises opportunities for meaningful cross-curricular links and purposeful learning experiences. We believe in learning which combines fun activities with a more formal approach, introducing our children to a wide range of knowledge and skills, equipping them for the modern world.
Children in year 6 are well prepared for the challenges they face in secondary school selection tests, Key Stage 3 and beyond. Our teachers are responsive to individual children’s needs and interests, working within a detailed framework based on the National Curriculum.
Art
Children are given opportunities to explore their ideas by experimenting, inventing and creating their own works of art using a range of materials. They learn a variety of skills, including how to draw, paint and sculpt.
Design Technology
Our Design and Technology curriculum develops children’s skills and knowledge in design, structures, mechanisms, electrical control and a range of materials, including food.
Early Years Foundation Stage
Our Early Years Curriculum has numeracy and literacy as its heart. It is led by creative staff who help the children grow both cognitively and socially.
English Reading
Reading is one of the most important skills we teach our children. It is a life-skill that enables them to explore ideas and gain information as the basis for other learning, and to gain access to a myriad of worlds through stories and poems.
English Speaking & Listening
Speaking and listening skills are prioritised throughout the school, not only in literacy lessons but throughout the curriculum as children learn to listen and talk in many ways including discussions, presentations and role play.
English Writing
The power of effective writing is immense in that it allows us to properly communicate – to inform, persuade, convince, entertain and evoke emotions.
French
French is taught at Eastcourt from Year 1, by a specialist teacher. Lessons are active, with a large proportion of orally-based activities which relate to children’s lives. There is also a Spanish Club for younger children who want an earlier introduction to the subject.
Geography
The aim of Geography is to instill in children a curiosity and fascination about the world, its places and people. They are introduced to geographical information and vocabulary as part of a planned sequence of learning relating facts to each other to build a web of knowledge.
History
Our main aim is to create an interesting scheme of work, helping children to learn the importance of skills as well as knowledge. We introduce children to the fact that a world existed before they, and those around them, were born. We know what it was like from the evidence left behind, but often there are not enough clues to tell us the full story, so we have to do our best to complete the picture.
Computing
This subject is taught by an ICT specialist teacher. We aim to prepare children for life in a digital world where computers and technology have an ever-changing role to play. As the children develop, we hope that they will become more independent in their use of technology.
Maths
We believe Mathematics is a fascinating subject which has something to appeal to everyone. The aim of our daily lessons is to promote curiosity and encourage our children to grow into confident learners.
Music
Music lessons are led by a specialist teacher. The curriculum provides opportunities for children to participate in music-making activities as they listen to, perform and compose real music from a range of genres, cultures and styles.
PSHE
The curriculum is built on the fact children need to be aware of themselves and the world around them, open to learning and questioning values and beliefs in an open-ended way. Their social development is helped by building a sense of identity in a multi-cultural society.
Performing Arts
Our Performing Arts curriculum is designed to develop confidence and concentration – playing games and taking part in different forms of story telling. It comprises of interrelated activities which explore feelings, knowledge and ideas, leading to understanding. It explores themes and issues, creates a safe context in which to do so, and provides opportunities to reflect on the insights gained in the process. It draws on the knowledge, interests and enthusiasm of the child.
Physical Education
Our PE curriculum is designed so children take part in different sports which provide them with a sequential programme of skills. They are also encouraged to value fair play and respect.
Religious Education
As a school we aim to use a variety of active approaches, linked in some cases to other subjects, to explore various religious and non-religious perspectives on issues relevant to our children; providing opportunities for reflection and spiritual development.They learn to recognise the difference between right and wrong through the study of moral and ethical questions. Exploring issues of religious faith and value, they develop their knowledge and understanding of the cultural context of their own lives.
Science
In Science we focus on practical activities to explore, develop and consolidate scientific ideas, skills, knowledge and understanding.As a result, by the time the children reach Year 5 they are ready to move from science topics into the 3 explicit areas of Biology, Chemistry and Physics.
Non Verbal Reasoning
Pattern recognition and codes which rely on logic and thinking out of the box provide a different sort of challenge from that presented in other subjects. The aim is to assess children’s visual acuity, speed of perception, and ability to recognise and manipulate objects.
